svg.text: Keyboard robot: solenoid driver with a TC4420 gate driver
Pro Micro D9 (OUT) → TC4420 → MOSFET → solenoid. Non-inverting: D9 HIGH = solenoid pulled in. All grounds are one net.

g.text: tie both VDD pins (1, 8) to +12 V
tie both GND pins (4, 5) to ground

svg.text: D9 only has to swing the TC4420 input (VIH ≥ 2.4 V, VIL ≤ 0.8 V, ±10 µA). The driver then charges the MOSFET gate to the full 12 V in ≈ 0.1 µs (6 A peak, 25 ns typ. edges into 2.5 nF), so Q1 switches hard and cleanly.

R1 = 1 kΩ: the input may not take more than 50 mA when it is above VDD (driver unpowered, D9 high). R2 holds IN low at reset. Do not add an RC filter: slow edges can double-pulse the output (datasheet §3.2).
R3 (10 Ω, use 4.7 – 22 Ω) damps ringing; the gate current peaks at ≈ 12 V / (10 Ω + 2.5 Ω) ≈ 1 A, well under 6 A. R4 keeps the gate low if the driver has no supply.
With D1 alone the coil current decays over tens of ms. With Z1 in series the drain rises to ≈ 12 V + 24 V + 0.4 V ≈ 36 V and the current collapses in a few ms (Q1 must be rated ≥ 40 V).
Bypass VDD with ≥ 1 µF ceramic right at the pins (datasheet §3.1); keep the ground pins on very short traces to the supply return, and return the coil current there, not through the Pro Micro.
VDD must stay ≤ 18 V (20 V absolute maximum): with a 24 V solenoid supply, feed the TC4420 from a separate 12 V.
